newsitem.title: CHINA: China not encouraging on refining - Mobil.
newsitem.headline: China not encouraging on refining - Mobil.

text.p: Mobil Corp is continuing discussions with Chinese officials on possible oil refining projects, but Beijing is not encouraging the oil group, a senior Mobil official said on Saturday.
"We continue to talk to Chinese authorities on refining," said George Good, chairman of Mobil Oil China Investment Co Ltd, Mobil's holding company for its China operations.
"(But) We are not being encouraged today by China to participate in refining," Good said.
Good was speaking to reporters after ceremonies to mark the opening of Mobil's $45 million lubricant plant in the northern port city of Tianjin.
Good suggested that state refiner China National Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec) was reluctant to allow more foreign participation in refining in China.
"Sinopec feels it has the technology to upgrade its facilities," he said.
State Planning Commission chief Chen Jinhua said this week that China would look at proposals for refinery projects from foreign oil companies on a case-by-case basis.
However, he said that China was using only about 70 percent of its existing refining capacity and that Beijing wanted to prevent duplication of facilities.
Other planning commission officials have said they do not want additional capacity, particularily from small-scale refineries, before the year 2000.
